\newcommand{\anchorParagraph}{We registered anchor criteria before any anchor run (protocol 4.7): no configuration may beat the physical floor computed with STREAM Triad (A1); on an A100 x86 host the median error must be at most 25\% (A2) and the model must under-predict at least two thirds of the configurations, as on the A10 (A3). The predictor is the third-party fit with each machine's STREAM Triad and datasheet GPU bandwidth; each prediction file was committed by the job before the one that measured. The instance Lambda provided for the A100 test was the 80\,GB SXM4 card (host: 30 vCPUs of an EPYC 7J13, Triad 94\,GB/s). On 29 \texttt{--n-cpu-moe} configurations of six GGUF files (Mixtral-8x7B at Q4\_K\_M and Q8\_0; Phi-3.5-MoE, Qwen2-57B-A14B and Qwen3-30B-A3B at Q4\_K\_M; DeepSeek-V2-Lite at Q8\_0), A2 fails (median error 34\%) and A3 holds: the model under-predicts 25 of 29, and with experts offloaded llama.cpp runs a median 1.46$\times$ (up to 1.96$\times$) faster than predicted. A1 fails as registered: 7 configurations beat the floor computed with STREAM Triad, by up to 16\%, so llama.cpp's expert kernels read host memory faster than Triad's read-write mix reports; against datasheet peaks (205\,GB/s DRAM), the basis of the audit's speed-of-light, every configuration stays below 54\%. Time per token is affine in the CPU layers ($R^2\ge0.970$). On a GH200 VM (64 Grace cores, LPDDR5X, NVLink-C2C; Triad 301\,GB/s), a platform outside the fitted envelope, the same 29 configurations show two regimes. With experts on the CPU (25 configurations) the model under-predicts 20 of them (measured/predicted 0.55--1.50, median error 23\%), the conservative direction seen on the A10; the exceptions are every DeepSeek-V2-Lite configuration and one Qwen3 one (5 in all). All-GPU runs (4) are over-predicted, measured/predicted 0.28--0.92: at 4\,TB/s a small model's decode step is dominated by per-layer fixed costs that Eq.~(1) omits. Over all 29, the median error is 24\%; no configuration exceeds the Triad-based floor (the closest reaches 86\% of it, and 51\% of the datasheet-peak one), and time per token is affine in the CPU layers ($R^2\ge0.997$). These statistics use the registered STREAM-based inputs; \cref{sec:audit} compares the same runs with the audit's datasheet-based predictions.}
